title: Heathers video:@Joe Weinberg  Ben’s video:@Broadway Ben  #broadway #m...
transcript: Okay, I can admit when I'm wrong because Titanique is coming to Broadway, but just a few weeks ago, I said this: That video, which is linked in the caption was not about Titanique, it was about Heather's. But I phrased it as a generalization. But Titanique is an exception to what I said, so what gives? I still stand by a lot of what I said in that video. Partly that 95% of the time, I still think I would be correct in predicting that a commercial off-Broadway run won't go to Broadway, but also in the sense that I still think that shows like Titanique and Heathers would have a very difficult time being profitable on Broadway. But obviously I was wrong in the sense that if you'd ask me if this was gonna happen, I would have been like, “no way.” So in retrospect, do I now think Heathers has more of a chance to move to Broadway? I mean, on some level, sure? Because, like, we are in the midst of a commercial off Broadway renaissance. We haven't necessarily reached a new normal. So pattern recognition can only take me so far. Like, ultimately, there are no rules, and producers have done much stupider and much more surprising things than this. But for what it's worth, I still don't think Heathers is going to Broadway, and here's why I think it's different from Titanique: I *would* have said that Titanique is almost less likely than Heathers to go to Broadway because they already experienced a drop off in demand. They didn't necessarily fail I don't know if it recouped or not, but it was like a “game over.” Like ending a game of Pac Man with a nice respectable score, but you're still out of lives. But with this new information, it seems like maybe their mentality is more like “let's play a different game.” Seems like their bid to become a long running staple off-Broadway didn't exactly work out. So as Broadway Ben said in his video this morning, which I'll also link in the caption, it seems like maybe they're trying to cement their legacy through licensing now by basically rebranding it as a potentially Tony winning Broadway show. But Heather's still doesn't have even that incentive because they've already cemented their legacy very successfully through a different route. So even having conceded that, commercial off Broadway shows have maybe more paths to Broadway than I originally acknowledged. I still don't see how Heathers specifically would benefit from a transfer. Cause like going back to the arcade metaphor: Even if Titanique lost their game of Pac Man, at least they were at a crossroads point to decide whether to play again or go home. But why would Heather start putting quarters in a different machine when their first game of Pac Man is still going strong?
